about: Cars researched but held back from the game because one figure could not be sourced to the rules in docs/DATA_GUIDE.md. Nothing in this folder is loaded by the game or the validator.

cars.missing: A US curb weight from a qualifying source (manufacturer page, major magazine spec panel, or two independent editorial outlets that agree).

confirmed.powerQuote: The first M3 produced 192 hp from its 2.3-liter four-cylinder engine during its 1988-1991 model year run.

weightCandidates.source: Grassroots Motorsports project-car panel (auto-filled, contains errors)

cars.notes: BMW Group Classic gives production 1986-1990 and only the European 1,200 kg. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weak sources disagree by about 4.8% (Carscoops, eightiescars, ultimatespecs about 2,735 lb; iSeeCars, Grassroots Motorsports, strictlyeta about 2,865 lb), so it stays held.

cars.missing: A curb weight from a second source or a magazine spec panel, and Ford's own release read on a Ford or press site (it was found only as a forum copy).

weightCandidates.source: duPont Registry (Edward Jones, 25 Jan 2024), not labelled curb

cars.notes: Hagerty's buyer's guide gives 2,027 cars for 2005 and 2,011 for 2006. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weak sources disagree by about 4% (Edmunds 3,475 lb; Cars.com and KBB 3,350 lb; duPont Registry 3,485 lb unlabelled), so it stays held.

cars.missing: A settled curb weight and US model years. Three kerb figures exist: 1,480 kg (Evo panel, used in the draft), 1,365 kg (usually attributed to Ferrari, seen only in auto-filled panels) and 3,230 lb (Hagerty, US car). The draft record is EU-market with calendar years 2002-2004, unlike the other Ferraris; US model years were not sourced.
cars.notes: 660 cv = 651 hp (ferrari.com magazine article). 6-speed automated manual, V12 5,998 cc, dry weight 1,255 kg per Ferrari. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: two named-author outlets (auto.cz, Michal Razim; km77, Victor M. Fernandez) give a kerb weight of 1,365 kg, which conflicts with Evo's panel figure of 1,480 kg (8% apart, both step 2); stays held until one is shown to be right. US model year appears to be 2003 only (EPA via MPG Buddy, Hagerty).

cars.missing: A qualifying curb weight. Ferrari's release gives no weight, and the four magazine figures found disagree.

confirmed.powerQuote: Total maximum power: 963 CV (Ferrari Geneva 2013 release, reproduced at https://www.2luxury2.com/?p=45214 and https://www.supercars.net/blog/?p=370141); 963 x 0.98632 = 950 hp

weightCandidates.source: 1,255 kg dry (supercars.net, rossoautomobili.com); not seen on a Ferrari page
1,410 kg, Motor Sport, Andrew Frankel: 'a proper, comparable with fluids kerb weight' https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/july-2014/62/laferrari
1,430 kg, MOTOR (Australia) spec panel, Georg Kacher https://whichcar.com.au/reviews/ferrari-laferrari-review

cars.notes: 499 built; calendar years 2013-2016 from one unsigned source. US model years not sourced. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: KBB 2,976 lb vs magazines 1,410-1,430 kg (3,109-3,153 lb); stays held. US model years: EPA via MPG Buddy rates 2014 only; KBB also lists 2015.

weightCandidates.source: GM table via GM Authority, marked (est.)
Car and Driver measured test weight, manual coupe (via cadillacvnet)

cars.notes: The sedan may have ended after 2018; not confirmed. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: databases disagree by about 3% (coupe: KBB 3,700 vs Cars.com 3,803 lb; sedan: Edmunds 3,700 vs Cars.com 3,812 lb), so it stays held. GM's 3,700 lb is 'est.'.

cars.missing: A final curb weight. Dodge's 2021 sheet gives 5,710 lb and the 2023 sheet 5,575 lb, both under 'WEIGHTS (Estimates)'.
cars.notes: Confirmed: 710 hp, 6,166 cc supercharged V8, 8-speed automatic, full-time AWD (2021 sheet, s3.amazonaws.com/chryslermedia.iconicweb.com/mediasite/specs/2021_DG_Durango_DurangoSRT_SP.pdf). Model years 2021, then 2023 onward (no 2022); still listed for 2027. Owner found Car and Driver's specifications page (https://www.caranddriver.com/dodge/durango/specs, 2026 Durango); its curb weight for the SRT Hellcat trim would qualify at step 2 (the 4,875 lb found there is the GT RWD). Car and Driver's specifications page (https://www.caranddriver.com/dodge/durango/specs) would qualify if its SRT Hellcat trim shows a curb weight (the owner's first figure, 4,875 lb, was for the GT RWD). 3 October 2026 provisional pass: Dodge's estimate (5,710 lb) and Car and Driver's tested 5,534 lb disagree by 3.2%; stays held.

cars.missing: Any Tesla horsepower rating and curb weight; Tesla did not publish hp for these years.
cars.notes: 3 October 2026 provisional pass: horsepower sources disagree widely (450-487 hp) and 2021 weights disagree (Cars.com 4,250 vs KBB 4,065 lb); stays held. 2018 weight 4,072 lb (Cars.com and KBB) agrees.

cars.missing: Rivian horsepower and any qualifying curb weight.
cars.notes: MotorWeek: 835 hp total. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weights disagree by 2.9% (7,148 vs 6,949 lb); 835 hp everywhere but no Rivian page. A future record should cover only the Gen 1 Quad (2022-2024).

cars.missing: A curb weight from GM or a major magazine. GM Heritage kits exist but are image scans; CorvSport's 3,465 lb is one outlet.
cars.notes: Confirmed (Chevrolet release reproduced by Corvette Action Center): 375 hp 1990-1992, 405 hp 1993-1995, 5.7-liter LT5; reference year would be 1990. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weights disagree by about 5% (CorvSport 3,465 lb manual 1990; Vette registry 3,330 lb), so it stays held. Power confirmed by Chevrolet's ZR1 history release (corvetteactioncenter.com/specs/c6/2009/zr1/2009_zr1_press4.html).
